text.House Cat: Visit a player and lay an egg in their nest. Learn their role and who they visited.
text.Goose: In the round the Goose is revealed, winners are losers and losers are winners during scoring. Visit a player: lay an egg in their nest and both their neighbours' nests.
text.Pelican: Visit a player. All players that visit you visit that player instead. Lay an egg for every redirected visitor. The player you visit is never redirected, even if they visit you.
text.Maine Coon: Visit a player. During the day, before anyone has called CAW CAW, you may stand up, bet any number of cards from your nest, and guess each player's animal. If you are correct, you win exclusively. Otherwise, you lose exclusively.
text.Lyrebird: Visit a player. Lay eggs in your nest equal to the number of eggs laid in their nest tonight.
text.Cassowary: Visit a player at night. If any eggs were laid in their nest tonight, kill them.
text.Brumby: Visit a player. Roles will rotate clockwise equal to the number of eggs laid in their nest tonight.
text.Ugly Duckling: You appear as Meowfia to investigators. Visit a player and steal the eggs laid in their nest tonight.

notes: A dead player can still be eggsecuted. The round is then scored on that player's side as usual.
Everyone draws 2 cards at setup, before the night. Compare nests with their size after that draw: only the change overnight is evidence.
Animals and sides are dealt afresh every round. What a player was last round says nothing about this round.

review.headline: The Top Cat flipped someone every round, and the deck ran dry.
review.summary: Farm won the first two rounds easily. The table caught a cagey Top Cat (Alex) and then a Top Cat who joked "I'm Top Cat... kidding" (Blair). In round 3 the deck was empty, so eggs stopped showing up as cards. A Top Cat flip plus a Switcheroo swap left three Meowfia at the table. The Meowfia piled onto Blair, an honest Mosquito, and won. Ellis won on 66, mostly from one banked throw of 12, 13 and 13 in round 1.

rounds.recap: Alex (Top Cat) flipped Casey, the Lorikeet, to Meowfia. Four visitors got Winks, which confirmed Casey's claim. Alex dodged claiming a role for two beats, then pushed the one verified player. That sank him, and Alex was eggsecuted as Meowfia in a 5-way pile-on.

Blair (Top Cat) flipped Drew, then let slip "I'm Top Cat... kidding" and changed stories. Drew read the slip, guessed Blair had flipped him, and shook hands on the Golden Wattle for +3 each. The table still eggsecuted Blair as Meowfia.

The deck was empty, so every nest showed +0 and egg evidence vanished. Ellis's Top Cat flipped Drew, and Alex's Switcheroo then swapped Drew's and Finley's animals, leaving three Meowfia. Farm players misread the empty-deck +0 as proof that Blair's Mosquito claim was false. Blair, who was Farm, was eggsecuted, and Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Four players visited the Lorikeet and each got a Wink, which turned the Lorikeet into a confirmed role. Nobody knew the Top Cat had already flipped Casey to Meowfia.
Blair's "I'm Top Cat... kidding" lost Blair the round. It also told Drew who had flipped him, and Drew used that to bond with Blair for +3 each.
Alex worked out that his Emu was really a Pigeon, because every other Farm animal in the pool had been claimed. That explained Blair's stray egg.
Casey said "Meowfia is among Alex, Drew, Ellis, Finley", which was exactly right. The table ignored her and eggsecuted the honest Mosquito.

confusions.what: Said an Ugly Duckling "steals eggs, it doesn't gain them". In fact the Duckling gains the eggs it steals, so Blair's +2 was correct.
Repeated the same mistake and called Blair's +2 inconsistent with Ugly Duckling.
Counted Casey's three eggs as coming from Ellis, Drew and Alex. Alex was a Top Cat and laid nothing. The third egg was Casey's own Lorikeet egg.
Pushed a Nobody bet because there were "no stray eggs". That ignores that a Top Cat leaves no egg trail.
As a flipped Meowfia, rated Alex 75% likely Meowfia, then threw at him anyway. A throw at your own teammate loses and gets no card back.
Threw at Ellis believing Ellis was Farm, to get a card back if he lost. Ellis was a Meowfia teammate, so no card came back.
Called Blair's Mosquito claim "provably" false because no nest changed. With an empty deck, laid eggs never show. Casey had also said she was confused, which is exactly what a Mosquito does.
Said a Wink from the Lorikeet "doesn't fit a random visit". A random visit to the Lorikeet does give a Wink. This may have been a deliberate Meowfia lie, but nobody corrected it.
Argued that Casey's visit should have affected him. A Lorikeet visit does nothing to its target.
Said "I'm going Bottlebrush", then threw at Alex instead.

design_notes: The deck ran out by round 3. Laid eggs then showed as +0 on the public change list, while private reports still said an egg was laid. This erased the main evidence and caused the Farm loss. Add a reshuffle, a bigger deck, or a public count of eggs laid. Casey's report also printed a blank card ("You drew ."), and the nest-size line was printed twice.
Six Winks were handed out, and nobody ever used one. The Lorikeet only worked as a way to confirm a role. Winks need a reason to be used, or a cost for not using them.

The Top Cat was in play and flipped someone in all three rounds. A flip combined with a swap broke the 2-Meowfia cap (3 Meowfia in round 3). It is the most common and most swingy cat. Consider limiting it or warning the table when the cap is broken.

Golden Wattle made the best moment of the game: Drew used a slip of the tongue to find his teammate. Bottlebrush and the Chicken's single-egg loss rule never mattered. Nobody threw at the flower, and the Chicken ended up on a Meowfia nobody threw at.

Card values decide too much. Ellis's single throw of 12, 13 and 13 in round 1 (38 points) was the winning margin by itself. Every vote was a near-unanimous pile-on, so the betting rarely added any tension.
